headline: Blue Cross Blue Shield ties $942 million in extra billing to AI-assisted coding
body: Blue Cross Blue Shield Association estimated that AI-assisted hospital coding contributed to nearly $942 million in extra costs for its health plans between 2023 and 2025, with about 70%, or $653 million, tied to extra diagnoses that did not change a patient's care. BCBSA's Luke Chalker said "multiple factors contribute to coding intensity," but added that the findings suggest AI-enabled coding tools are playing a role.
note: Hospital coding is one example of a wider pattern: when AI speeds up a process built on an existing financial incentive, it can scale whatever bias is already in the system as easily as it scales efficiency, which is a caution for AI-driven credit and claims models too.

figure.label: extra costs BCBSA linked to AI-assisted hospital coding, 2023-2025

evidence.text: Blue Cross Blue Shield Association recently estimated that hospitals' use of AI-assisted medical coding contributed to close to $1 billion ( $942 million ) in additional costs for its health plans between 2023 and 2025.

Roughly 70%, or $653 million of the billing identified by the insurer, was tied to additional diagnoses that were not accompanied by a change in care, Luke Chalker, BCBSA's senior vice president of product and data science, told CNBC.

Chalker stopped short of attributing the entire increase to AI. "While multiple factors contribute to coding intensity, the findings suggest AI-enabled coding and documentation tools are playing a role," he said.
